english.title: Damage / top / lop a tree in a conservation area in a manner likely to destroy it
english.standardoffencewording: On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) in a conservation area, namely **(..SPECIFY THE CONSERVATION AREA..), designated by **(..SPECIFY THE AUTHORITY..), wilfully damaged, topped or lopped a tree at **(..SPECIFY THE LOCATION..) in such a manner as to be likely to destroy it
english.legislation: Contrary to section 211(1) and 210(1) of the Town and Country Planning Act 1990.
english.pointstoprove:
date and location
in conservation area designated by an authority
wilfully damaged, topped or lopped a tree
in such a manner as to be likely to destroy it

investigatoraction.description: Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes:
(i) Section 211(3) of the Town and Country Planning Act 1990 provides that it shall be a defence for a person charged with an offence under section 211(1) to prove -
(a) that he served notice of his intention to do the act in question (with sufficient particulars to identify the tree) on the local planning authority in whose area the tree is or was situated; and
(b) that he did the act in question with the consent of the local planning authority in whose area the tree is or was situated, or
after the expiry of the period of six weeks from the date of the notice but before the expiry of the period of two years from that date.
(ii) See H10810 for the either way offence where the offender has caused another person to damage, top or lop a tree in a conservation area.
(iii) See H10811 for the either way offence where the offender has permitted a tree in a conservation area to be damaged, topped or lopped.
(iv) See H10812 for the either way offence where the offender has cut down / uprooted / wilfully destroyed a tree in a conservation area.
(v) See H10813 for the either way offence where the offender has caused another person to cut down / uproot / wilfully destroy a tree in a conservation area.
(vi) See H10814 for the either way offence where the offender has permitted another person to cut down / uproot / wilfully destroy a tree in a conservation area.
(vii) See H7225 for the either way offence where a tree subject of a tree preservation order is cut down, uprooted, destroyed etc.
(viii) See H7219 for the either way offence where a tree subject of a tree preservation order is damaged, lopped or topped.
(ix) See H7229 for the summary offence where a tree subject of a tree preservation order is otherwise damaged.
(x) In determining the amount of any fine to be imposed on a person convicted of an offence under section 210(1) the court shall in particular have regard to any financial benefit which has accrued or appear likely to accrue to him in consequence of the offence.

other.penalty:
Summary: A fine not exceeding £20,000.
Indictment: A fine.

Time limit for prosecutions:
None

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates' court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
